context: Add a support_status column to platforms list, sourced from the registry the same way benchmarks does it, and rename the existing column to something that says what it means (Driver / Installed / Available). Do not change the taxonomy in public-contracts.md - it is correct and test-enforced. Consider a second, separate signal for whether a platform has ever produced a published result, which is a different question again from both columns.
description: docs/reference/public-contracts.md defines the support taxonomy correctly and warns explicitly that support_status 'is different from local dependency availability: a stable platform can be unavailable on a developer machine because an optional SDK is not installed'. The CLI then breaks exactly that distinction. 'benchbox platforms list' prints a column headed 'Status' whose values are dependency availability ('Enabled' when the driver imports), and it never shows support_status at all - grep for support_status across benchbox/cli/ returns no platform-side hit. Benchmarks already do this correctly: benchbox/cli/benchmarks.py renders 'Support: <status>' from registry metadata. So this is a parity gap on the platform surface, not a taxonomy problem. Registry today: stable=5, beta=28, experimental=17, deprecated=1. Users choosing among 51 platforms currently get no runtime signal that Onehouse Quanton is experimental and DuckDB is stable.

verifications.description: Platform support status reaches the CLI
verifications.expected: shows support status distinct from driver availability
